learningObjective: Understand that a circle can be decomposed into many thin concentric rings stacked from center outward — the circle isn't a solid blob but layers from the center out
ahaMoment: The circle isn't a solid blob but rather dozens or hundreds of thin rings stacked together, each contributing a small amount to the total area

miniSpec.title: Drag Radius to Grow Concentric Rings
miniSpec.manipulated_variable: Dragging the endpoint of a radius line outward from the center, which changes the current radius value r
miniSpec.primary_visual_feedback: Concentric rings appear sequentially inside the swept area, with each new ring appearing at the current radius position as the handle moves outward
miniSpec.goal_structure: Free exploration with optional encouragement to drag fully from center to edge to see the complete decomposition
miniSpec.causal_chain_exposed: The current radius value r displayed numerically, the number of rings shown so far, and optionally the thickness of each ring (dr) labeled on one ring
miniSpec.trace_strategy: All previously-drawn rings remain visible and accumulate, creating a full disk; no erasure occurs because the concept requires seeing the complete buildup of layers
miniSpec.aha_moment: The circle isn't a solid blob but rather dozens or hundreds of thin rings stacked together, each contributing a small amount to the total area

modelVariables.rings_currentRadius: current radius position r (0 to R_max), student-dragged outward from center
modelVariables.rings_ringCount: derived: number of rings that have been painted so far, based on currentRadius / dr
modelVariables.rings_maxRadius: the full circle's radius R (fixed), shown as the outer boundary

assertions.description: On load, the circle is empty (no rings yet) — the handle sits near the center, inviting the student to drag outward
assertions.visualCheck: Circle outline visible but interior mostly empty; handle visible at center

assertions.description: Dragging the radius outward causes rings to appear and accumulate
assertions.visualCheck: Multiple concentric rings fill the circle from center to the dragged position

assertions.description: Dragging to the maximum radius fills the entire circle with rings
assertions.visualCheck: Circle is completely filled with concentric rings from center to edge

invariants.description: The number of rings shown is proportional to the current radius
